title: Worksheet 15: The History of ENIAC
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: ENIAC, which stands for Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer, was completed in 1945 and is widely considered one of the first general-purpose electronic computers, meaning it could be reprogrammed to solve different types of problems rather than being built to do just one specific task. ENIAC was enormous compared to modern computers, filling an entire room and weighing about 30 tons, using nearly 18,000 vacuum tubes to perform calculations. Unlike modern computers, which can be programmed using a keyboard, reprogramming ENIAC to solve a different problem required physically rewiring the machine by hand, plugging and unplugging cables and flipping switches, a process that could take days. ENIAC was originally built for the United States Army to calculate artillery firing tables, but it was also later used for early research related to the hydrogen bomb. Notably, ENIAC's programming team was made up mainly of women, including Kay McNulty, Betty Jennings, and several others, who are now recognized as among the first computer programmers in history, even though their contributions went largely uncredited for decades.
